jsonBlocks.title: prepare-ebs.sh
jsonBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT_SOURCE=$(findmnt -n -o SOURCE /)
ROOT_PARENT=$(lsblk -no PKNAME "$ROOT_SOURCE" | head -n1)

DATA_DEV=$(lsblk -dpno NAME,TYPE | awk '$2=="disk"{print $1}' | grep -v "/dev/${ROOT_PARENT}" | head -n1)

if [ -z "${DATA_DEV}" ]; then
  echo "No non-root EBS data disk was detected."
  exit 1
fi

sudo mkfs.xfs -f "${DATA_DEV}"
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/ebs
sudo mount "${DATA_DEV}" /mnt/ebs

echo "fa-s3-storage encrypted EBS snapshot training file" | sudo tee /mnt/ebs/ebs-training.txt
sudo sync

sudo cat /mnt/ebs/ebs-training.txt
lsblk -f

jsonBlocks.title: unmount-ebs.sh
jsonBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

sudo sync
sudo umount /mnt/ebs

#!/bin/bash

tasks.goal: Launch fa-s3-storage-client-a and fa-s3-storage-client-b with no SSH key and the EFS/XFS packages installed by user data.
tasks.whyItMatters: The clients prove AZ-scoped EBS behavior and multi-AZ EFS shared access without opening inbound administrative ports.

consoleSteps.title: Launch one SSM-managed EC2 storage client in each Availability Zone

instructions.text: Open EC2.
Launch fa-s3-storage-client-a using Amazon Linux 2023, t3.micro, subnet fa-s3-storage-public-a, fa-s3-storage-ec2-sg, no key pair and instance profile fa-s3-storage-ec2-profile.
Under Advanced details paste instance-user-data.sh.
Launch fa-s3-storage-client-b with the same settings except subnet fa-s3-storage-public-b.
Wait for both EC2 status checks to pass.

consoleSteps.title: Review the SAA-C03 storage and backup decision points
consoleSteps.instruction: EBS: AZ-scoped block storage for EC2; choose volume family based on latency, IOPS, throughput and cost.

instructions.text: EBS: AZ-scoped block storage for EC2; choose volume family based on latency, IOPS, throughput and cost.
EBS snapshots: point-in-time backups; restore by creating a new volume. Encrypted source volumes create encrypted snapshots.
EFS Regional: shared NFS file system with data stored across multiple AZs; mount targets provide VPC NFS endpoints.
EFS access point: application-specific root and POSIX identity boundary on the same file system.
FSx Windows: SMB/Active Directory.
FSx Lustre: high-performance parallel Linux/POSIX workloads and S3 integration.
FSx ONTAP: NetApp and multi-protocol NFS/SMB/iSCSI/NVMe requirements.
FSx OpenZFS: managed OpenZFS for NFS workloads.
AWS Backup plan: policy/schedule/lifecycle; backup selection: protected resources; recovery point: stored backup artifact.
Glacier Instant Retrieval: immediate access; Flexible/Deep Archive use restore workflows and different retrieval speeds.
Storage Gateway: hybrid file, block or virtual-tape interface to AWS storage.
Exam trigger: one EC2 database data disk -> EBS; multiple Linux hosts sharing the same files -> EFS.
Exam trigger: Windows SMB/AD -> FSx Windows; HPC + S3 dataset -> FSx Lustre.
Exam trigger: centrally scheduled multi-service backups -> AWS Backup.
Exam trigger: archive retrieval in minutes -> Flexible Retrieval Expedited; hours and lowest urgency -> Standard/Bulk or Deep Archive based on retention/retrieval need.
